name: Teen testosterone-for-facial-structure belief

lead: Some teenagers in looksmaxxing spaces believe that increasing testosterone or other hormones while still growing will push the jaw, brow and cheekbones toward a more masculine shape. The claimed payoff is a face with stronger bone structure.

Puberty does reshape the face and body, and androgens drive many male changes, so the idea builds on a real process. Medical references also describe estrogen as the hormone that closes growth plates, and anabolic steroid references report that adolescent use can stop bone lengthening early.

paras: In forums the belief appears as questions and plans about hormones, boosters or steroids by minors. Replies on T Nation to a 16-year-old asking about a cycle list reasons against, including disruption of hormonal development.

Anabolic steroids in adolescents are reported to prematurely close growth plates, reduce adult height potential, and suppress natural testosterone production. These substances are controlled or prescription-only in many countries, and paediatric endocrinologists manage hormone treatment for diagnosed conditions such as delayed puberty.

angle.text: Believers expect extra androgens in the teen years to enlarge and sharpen facial bone. Medical references link the effects of adolescent hormones mainly to growth-plate maturation and puberty timing.

lead: The teen testosterone-for-facial-structure belief is the notion, held by some adolescents, that raising hormone levels during puberty will remodel facial bones into a more masculine form. It draws on the observable fact that puberty changes faces and bodies.

Reference sources describe estradiol as the principal hormone driving the pubertal growth spurt and growth-plate closure, and androgens as driving voice change and facial hair.[1] Anabolic steroid references report that use before growth ends can prematurely stop bone lengthening, affect natural hormone production, and cause acne and other effects.[2]
On T Nation a user asking about a first anabolic steroid cycle at age 16 received replies listing disrupted hormonal development among the reasons against.[3]

paras: Proponents argue that the window of adolescence is when bone shape is set and that more hormone means more development. Discussions overlap with androgen maxxing and with height concerns.

Puberty references describe sex differences in height arising from the later, longer male growth spurt and lower estradiol rise.[1] They do not describe a method of adding facial bone through supplemental hormones. Anabolic steroid references list premature growth-plate closure, suppression of the hormonal axis, and early puberty in boys among adolescent concerns.[2]
Replies in a T Nation thread with a minor asking about steroids cite disrupted hormonal development.[3] Medical references list acne, stretch marks and hair loss among androgenic effects.[2]
No studies found testing hormones to reshape adolescent facial bone for appearance. Paediatric endocrinology studies of hormones in diagnosed conditions are a separate, broader category.

lore.intro: The belief surfaces in teen questions about hormones and steroids on lifting and looksmaxxing forums.[3]

claims.claim: Extra hormones in the teen years build a more masculine facial skeleton.
